actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.name: ticks

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed

facts.text: DexJoCo is a MuJoCo-based simulation benchmark and toolkit for task-oriented dexterous manipulation with 11 functionally grounded tasks
The card's main model is the MJCF scene arena_arm_hand_bimanual_assembly.xml, whose root element is '<mujoco model="Arena_Allegro_Bimanual_Assembly">'
The assembly scene includes panda_allegro_bimanual.xml, industri_round_peg_8mm.xml and industreal_tray_insert_round_peg_8mm.xml
The assembly scene sets the physics timestep to 0.002 s
The assembly environment defines _XML_PATH as xmls/arena_arm_hand_bimanual_assembly.xml
The assembly environment passes _XML_PATH as xml_path to MujocoGymEnv
MujocoGymEnv loads the MJCF with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path and creates the data with mujoco.MjData
MujocoGymEnv sets the model time step from its physics_dt argument
The right arm has seven motor actuators: joints 1 to 4 have ctrlrange -87 to 87 and joints 5 to 7 have ctrlrange -12 to 12
The right hand has sixteen position actuators, four per finger, whose control ranges come from their default classes

The right hand control ranges are base -0.47 to 0.47, proximal -0.196 to 1.61, medial -0.174 to 1.709, distal -0.227 to 1.618, thumb base 0.263 to 1.396, thumb proximal -0.105 to 1.163, thumb medial -0.189 to 1.644 and thumb distal -0.162 to 1.719
The left model declares the same seven motor actuators and sixteen position actuators

The left hand control ranges are base -0.47 to 0.47, proximal -0.196 to 1.61, medial -0.174 to 1.709, distal -0.227 to 1.618, thumb base 0.263 to 1.396, thumb proximal -0.105 to 1.163, thumb medial -0.189 to 1.644 and thumb distal -0.162 to 1.719
The peg is a free body: its body element contains a freejoint
The tray insert is a free body: its body element contains a freejoint
The scene has two mocap target bodies, target_right and target_left
The assembly environment's reset samples the peg and socket positions, rotates their yaw and sets the Panda and Allegro home poses instead of the model defaults
The assembly environment's step takes a right and a left 23-value vector, a 7-value pose plus 16 hand commands per arm

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from the model defaults; the driver takes no seed, so a reset always returns to the same model state and a run repeats on the same engine. The fake backend is a deterministic stand-in, not MuJoCo.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the scene's MJCF text for the actuator control ranges, the free-joint layout and the qpos/qvel dimensions, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control target; it loads no mesh, texture, camera or sensor and resolves no contact, equality, tendon or actuator constraint

the driver serves the MJCF scene directly; the upstream task environment wraps it with a sampled reset (random peg and socket poses and table height), a 23-value pose-plus-hand vector per arm converted to actuator controls, a success predicate and camera observations (panda_bimanual_assembly_env.py:359-391, :432-455, :214-238); that task layer is not served
a reset restores the model defaults with mj_resetData and takes no seed, so it does not reproduce the environment's sampled start state or its domain randomization
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
the fake module does not implement mj_getState/mj_setState, so on the fake backend the bridge uses its time/qpos/qvel/ctrl snapshot rather than MuJoCo's full integration-state snapshot
no physical Panda or Allegro hardware is modelled and nothing was validated against it

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
